items.title: [Bug]: Yarn creates an unplugged package which is not needed on current OS (fsevents + node-gyp)
items.body:
### Self-service

- [ ] I'd be willing to implement a fix

### Describe the bug

My project has an indirect dependency on `fsevents`, which is a macOS only package. `fsevents` (apparently?) depends on `node-gyp`. Nothing else depends on `node-gyp`.

Yarn in PnP mode creates `.yarn/unplugged/node-gyp-npm-10.0.1-48708ce70b/`, even on Linux, where it should have no reason to download or unpack `node-gyp`.

### To reproduce

Run in a new empty directory:
```shellsession
$ echo {} > package.json
$ corepack yarn set version stable
$ corepack yarn add sass
➤ YN0000: · Yarn 4.0.2
➤ YN0000: ┌ Resolution step
➤ YN0085: │ + sass@npm:1.69.5, @isaacs/cliui@npm:8.0.2, @npmcli/agent@npm:2.2.0, @npmcli/fs@npm:3.1.0, @pkgjs/parseargs@npm:0.11.0, abbrev@npm:2.0.0, agent-base@npm:7.1.0, and 101 more.
➤ YN0000: └ Completed in 4s 225ms
➤ YN0000: ┌ Fetch step
➤ YN0000: └ Completed
➤ YN0000: ┌ Link step
➤ YN0000: │ ESM support for PnP uses the experimental loader API and is therefore experimental
➤ YN0000: └ Completed
➤ YN0000: · Done with warnings in 4s 476ms
$ ls -l
total 572K
-rwxr-xr-x 1 user user 453K Dec  1 02:58 .pnp.cjs*
-rw-r--r-- 1 user user  70K Dec  1 02:58 .pnp.loader.mjs
drwxr-xr-x 3 user user 4.0K Dec  1 02:58 .yarn/
-rw-r--r-- 1 user user   84 Dec  1 02:58 package.json
-rw-r--r-- 1 user user  34K Dec  1 02:58 yarn.lock
$ ls -l .yarn/
total 72K
-rw-r--r-- 1 user user  65K Dec  1 02:58 install-state.gz
drwxr-xr-x 3 user user 4.0K Dec  1 02:58 unplugged/
$ ls -l .yarn/unplugged/
total 4.0K
drwxr-xr-x 3 user user 4.0K Nov 28 22:21 node-gyp-npm-10.0.1-48708ce70b/
```

When PnP mode is disabled, you can see neither node_modules/fsevents nor node_modules/node-gyp is created, as expected:

### Self-service

### Describe the bug

This is basically a repeat of my request [that `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` should be the default](https://github.com/yarnpkg/yarn/issues/4147), now though with the `--immutable` flag instead.

Use case:

```
yarn init
yarn add moment
npm install --save lodash
yarn install
```

Now, running `yarn install` would mutate the lock as the `package.json` and  `yarn.lock` and are out of sync.

`yarn install --immutable` would provide an error.

(The usage of `npm` is a mistake in this workflow. Yet `yarn` should not resolve the package.json and mutate the lockfile by itself. yarn should error on the side of caution in order to ensure its claim to offer: 

> Safe, stable, reproducible projects

I still think that mutating the lockfile is something that yarn should almost never do, unless it is about adding or removing a dependency.

---

Though I also want to point out that berry does a lot of things better than the old yarn.

1.) `CI` env variable allows immutable implicitly. That is great!

I figured I could get my wanted behavior via:

```
CI=true yarn install
```

to force a default of `--immutable` without setting it.

2.) immutable can be set in `yarn.rc` AND overwritten  on the fly in order to sync the package

I added:

```yaml
enableImmutableInstalls: true
```

this makes all installs use immutable. If I want to sync the packages, I can use:

```
yarn install --no-immutable
```

to force the sync.

This means that having this setting in the each repo's `.yarnrc.yml` 

(This means that https://github.com/yarnpkg/yarn/issues/4570 was solved for berry.)

Though I was a bit surprised that I could use `--no-immutable`, as this is not part of the help, yet one can find it e.g. referenced [here](https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/discussions/3486#discussioncomment-1379344).

(I created a follow up to improve the docs / man pages: https://github.com/yarnpkg/berry/issues/7023 )

I do not have a minimal reproduction, but here's a failing CI job:
https://github.com/kaliber5/ember-bdd/actions/runs/885833497

It references a commit of a public open source project on GitHub.

I was able to work around the prpblem by setting the `YARN_ENABLE_IMMUTABLE_INSTALLS` env var to `false`. But it does not explain why Yarn is not able to use the lockfile.

**What's the problem this PR addresses?**
<!-- Describe the rationale of your PR. -->
<!-- Link all issues that it closes. (Closes/Resolves #xxxx.) -->

Resolving package metadata is slower than it has to be because, most times, Yarn has already fetched it in the past, and some things can be cached and reused.

This should improve performance in various cases (ranging from creating new projects and cache-only-but-no-lockfile installs to `yarn up` when no new versions are available), since the server can avoid resending the response body if nothing has changed.

**How did you fix it?**
<!-- A detailed description of your implementation. -->

This PR makes Yarn cache npm package metadata inside `<globalFolder>/metadata/npm/<cacheKey>/<registry>/<package>.json` when `getPackageMetadata` is used.

If an exact version is requested, Yarn will return the metadata from disk directly and avoid hitting the network altogether.

Otherwise, Yarn will set the `If-None-Match` & `If-Modified-Since` headers using the `etag` & `last-modified` values that were cached during previous requests. This tells the server to skip sending the response body and just respond with `304`, making Yarn reuse the cached metadata.
